llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 4.222 mg potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate from Quantos cartridge position 2 into the same experiment vial as the KCl. Subsequent 120-second stir-bar mixing dissolves the analyte in the prepared KCl electrolyte, producing 1.00 mM ferrocyanide in 0.100 M KCl.
assumptions: The available solid ferrocyanide cartridge contains potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate, K4[Fe(CN)6]·3H2O, molecular weight 422.388 g/mol. If the loaded material is anhydrous potassium ferrocyanide or another hydrate, the required mass must be recalculated before execution.
Water is available as a pump-compatible solvent on liquid channel 1.
KCl and potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate are physically loaded into the specified Quantos cartridge positions before execution.
The stated final volume is treated as the dispensed aqueous volume of 9.996 mL; dissolved-solid volume effects are neglected under standard solution-preparation convention.
No gas supply is explicitly identified as available; electrolyte purging is therefore not included.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: n = 0.100 mol/L × 0.009996 L = 0.0009996 mol. m = 0.0009996 mol × 74.5513 g/mol = 0.074521 g = 74.521 mg. Dispensing 74.521 mg into a final liquid volume of 9.996 mL produces 0.100 M KCl.

n = 0.00100 mol/L × 0.009996 L = 0.000009996 mol. m = 0.000009996 mol × 422.388 g/mol = 0.004222 g = 4.222 mg. Dispensing 4.222 mg into a final liquid volume of 9.996 mL produces 0.00100 M potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: The plan uses 2 solid cartridges, below the 8-cartridge limit, and 1 liquid channel, below the 4-channel limit. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg Quantos cartridge capacity: 74.521 mg KCl and 4.222 mg potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate. The 9.996 mL water volume is below the 10 mL vial limit and equals 1428 increments of 7 uL, so it is exactly representable by the liquid dispenser. One electrochemical slot is used, below the maximum of 3 parallel slots. Solids are assigned only to Quantos cartridges and water is assigned only to the compatible liquid pump.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No analyte deposition is performed; therefore no analyte-film drying step is required. The gold electrode is polished, washed, and dried before immersion in the prepared electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Not applicable: ferrocyanide is measured as a dissolved analyte in the electrolyte, not as a film or ink deposited on the gold working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the electrolyte directly in the experiment vial by Quantos dispensing 74.521 mg KCl, then liquid-pump dispensing 9.996 mL water through channel 1. The selected water volume is exactly compatible with the 7 uL pump increment. Add a stir bar and mix for 120 seconds after solid addition to dissolve KCl and establish a homogeneous 0.100 M KCl supporting electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl supporting electrolyte provides ionic conductivity while potassium is chemically compatible with potassium ferrocyanide. A 1.00 mM ferrocyanide concentration provides a readily measurable reversible ferricyanide/ferrocyanide redox response without requiring excessive analyte mass. The -0.10 V to +0.50 V window versus Ag/AgCl spans the expected ferrocyanide oxidation and ferricyanide reduction region while avoiding unnecessarily positive potentials on gold. A 0.050 V/s scan rate, 0.002 V step size, and three cycles provide initial conditioning followed by reproducible characterization scans. The physical sequence is: polish the gold working electrode; dispense KCl and potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate with Quantos into one experiment vial; dispense water with liquid-pump channel 1; stir for 120 seconds until homogeneous; install the vial in one electrochemical substation slot; perform the specified CV; then wash and dry electrodes and collect the solution as ferrocyanide-containing waste.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested ferrocyanide analyte is dissolved directly in an aqueous supporting electrolyte and measured in the experiment vial; therefore analite_in_electrolite is the applicable mode. No analyte deposition onto the gold working electrode is required.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry characterization of 1.00 mM potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate dissolved in 0.100 M potassium chloride aqueous supporting electrolyte using a gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.

cross_contamination_risks: Ferrocyanide residue on the gold electrode or electrochemical cell can affect subsequent redox experiments.
Rinse the working, counter, and reference-electrode-contact components according to the platform wash procedure after the measurement.
Use dedicated or thoroughly washed stir bars and experiment vials to prevent ferrocyanide carryover.
handling_precautions: Wear appropriate laboratory PPE, including gloves, splash-resistant eye protection, and a lab coat, during cartridge loading and vial handling.
Keep the ferrocyanide solution neutral to mildly basic; do not add acids and prevent contact with acidic waste.
Avoid generating or inhaling solid dust during Quantos cartridge loading.
Polish the gold working electrode, then wash and dry it before measurement to minimize carryover and obtain a reproducible electrode surface.
Mix for 120 seconds with a stir bar after all solids and water are dispensed, and visually verify dissolution before transferring the vial to the electrochemical substation.
hazards: Potassium ferrocyanide is a cyanide-complex salt and must not be acidified because strongly acidic conditions can promote release of toxic hydrogen cyanide.
Potassium chloride is a low-hazard inorganic salt but should be handled as laboratory chemical powder.
Electrical and mechanical hazards are present during electrode polishing and electrochemical-cell operation.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV ferrocyanide/KCl solution, rinses, and contaminated consumables in a labeled aqueous ferrocyanide/cyanide-complex waste container.
Do not combine ferrocyanide-containing waste with acidic waste or oxidizing waste streams.
Dispose of waste through the institution's approved hazardous-waste procedure.
